name: Heath Rocha
title: Superintendent, Los Gatos-Saratoga Union High School District
background: Rocha began his career as a school psychologist at a National Institutes of Health-funded drug treatment facility for adolescents. After earning his master's degree, he moved to California and started his education career in Monterey Peninsula Unified School District, then advanced through leadership roles at Carmel Unified School District as Coordinator, Director of Special Education, and Chief Student Services Officer. (Source: Los Gatos-Saratoga Union High School District, District Leadership.)

He joined Los Gatos-Saratoga Union High School District in 2016 and served nine years as Assistant Superintendent of Student Services before becoming Acting Superintendent for eight months and then permanent Superintendent. He holds a master's degree from the University of Vermont. (Source: Los Gatos-Saratoga Union High School District, District Leadership.)

During his tenure, the district credits him with establishing Wellness Centers at each of its high schools, associated with a reported 40% drop in students reporting persistent sadness over a two-week period, and with Title IX initiatives associated with a reported more-than-50% decrease in reported sexual harassment incidents; these are the district's own reported figures rather than independently audited statistics. He was named 2025–26 National Superintendent to Watch, per a news item referenced on the district's website, though I could not independently verify the awarding organization or criteria for that recognition within this session's tool budget. (Source: Los Gatos-Saratoga Union High School District website.)

As Superintendent, Rocha is one of the authors listed for Measure N, the district's November 2026 local funding measure, alongside Board President Theresa Bond, Vice President Katherine Tseng, Board Clerk Shawn Mortensen, and Trustee Steve Chen. (Source: scc-measure-n-2026.json in this voter guide.)
